cable.title: Persia’s royal mounted relay
cable.line: Herodotus describes Persian riders posted a day apart, passing messages hand to hand, so Xerxes’ news of Salamis raced to Susa.

cable.title: Ögedei builds the Mongol Yam
cable.line: Ögedei Khan set up staffed relay stations about every 25 miles, letting riders carry orders across Eurasia at up to 200 km a day.

crash.title: Amsterdam’s banking crisis of 1763
crash.line: A wartime credit boom breaks when the de Neufville bank fails, spreading bankruptcies to Hamburg and Prussia in an early cross-border crisis.

crash.title: The Panic of 1825
crash.line: A London boom in Latin American bonds and mines, even fictional Poyais, collapses; about 70 banks fail and borrowers across Latin America default.

dreadnought.title: The Arab fleet defeats Byzantium at sea
dreadnought.line: A caliphate fleet built in Syrian and Egyptian yards routs Emperor Constans II off Lycia, ending Byzantium’s unchallenged rule of the sea.

krakatoa.title: El Salvador’s Ilopango volcano erupts
krakatoa.line: A giant eruption buries Maya lands for 80 km and sends more sulfur aloft than Pinatubo, likely cooling the globe for years.

krakatoa.title: Iceland’s Eldgjá fissure eruption
krakatoa.line: Iceland’s largest lava flood veils Europe’s sun; 940 brings one of the coolest summers in 1,500 years, with hunger from Germany to China.

netscape.title: Britain’s Uniform Penny Post begins
netscape.line: A flat one-penny stamp made letters affordable to almost everyone, and the number sent in Britain more than doubled in the first year.

protests.title: Revolts erupt across Europe in the 1640s
protests.line: Catalonia and Portugal rose in 1640, Palermo and Naples in 1647, Paris in the 1648 Fronde, a wave historians call the General Crisis.

protests.title: The Revolutions of 1830
protests.line: France’s July Revolution was followed within months by revolts in Belgium, Poland, Switzerland and the Italian states.

saigon.title: Ming China withdraws from Đại Việt
saigon.line: After Lê Lợi’s rebels routed a 150,000-strong relief army in 1427, the besieged Ming garrison negotiated its retreat and left in early 1428.

saigon.title: Napoleon’s retreat from Moscow
saigon.line: Napoleon abandoned Moscow on 19 October 1812; cold, hunger and Cossack raids destroyed most of his Grande Armée on the way out.

springs.title: Amrita Devi dies defending trees
springs.line: Amrita Devi refused to let Marwar’s men fell khejri trees; 363 Bishnois died with her and the maharaja banned felling there.

springs.title: Marsh publishes Man and Nature
springs.line: George Perkins Marsh’s book warned that people were ruining the land, and it helped launch the conservation movement and national forests.

springtime.title: Spanish America’s juntas of 1810
springtime.line: With Napoleon holding Spain, Caracas, Buenos Aires, Bogotá and Santiago set up their own juntas within six months, and Hidalgo rose in Mexico.

sputnik.title: France launches the ironclad Gloire
sputnik.line: France launched Gloire, the first ocean-going ironclad, and alarmed Britain answered with the bigger iron-hulled HMS Warrior, starting a naval race.

trusts.title: Imperial diets curb the great trading houses
trusts.line: Diets at Nuremberg in 1522–24 passed laws capping trading companies’ capital and branches and banning one firm from controlling a commodity.

vaccine.title: Measles kills a child in New York
vaccine.line: An unvaccinated child dies of measles in Lewis County, New York’s first measles death in over 30 years, amid a 178-case outbreak.

triangle.title: The Pemberton Mill collapses
triangle.line: A Lawrence textile mill built on brittle cast-iron pillars collapses on its workers, killing between 88 and 145, many young immigrant women.

triangle.title: Thailand’s Kader toy factory fire
triangle.line: Fire at a Thai factory making toys for export kills 188 workers, mostly young women, more than died at Triangle.
